The secondary claim also fails: docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-cell-hf-wrap-affinity-todo.md:72-73 contains a checked step "Record where affinity is *produced* in docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md". The update is folded into the existing subsystem doc, not a parallel file, satisfying the design-doc discipline rule.

finding.summary: The getWrapAffinity half of the issue is only partially fixed: blocks inside a *nested* table cell still can never report 'forward'. getVisualLineRange's cell branch resolves `cellInfo.tableBlockId` against `layout.blocks` (top-level layout blocks only), so for a block inside a table nested in a cell the lookup misses, the fall-through `layout.blocks.find(pos.blockId)` also misses, and the function returns `[0, 0]` — making getWrapAffinity (line 4142) answer 'backward' unconditionally. The issue note states the defect as "cell-inner and header/footer blocks fall through to 'backward' after typing wraps a line", and the hit-test half of this PR was deliberately extended to arbitrary nesting depth via resolveOffsetInNestedTable, so the typing path is now inconsistent with the click path at depth ≥ 2.
finding.evidence: text-editor.ts:4058 `const tableLb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId);` — nested table blocks are not members of `layout.blocks`; contrast resolveOffsetInNestedTable (line 4901) which the PR does thread affinity through.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is misread: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4058` is not code but part of a comment block (lines 4056-4068) that explicitly documents the *removed* behavior ("an inner table is not a member of `layout.blocks`, so looking `cellInfo.tableBlockId` up there directly (as this used to) missed every block inside a nested cell, leaving `getWrapAffinity` stuck on 'backward'"). The reviewer quoted `const tableLb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId);` — no such statement exists anywhere in the file. The actual code at text-editor.ts:4071 is `const resolved = resolveNestedTableLayout(cellInfo.tableBlockId, layout);`, and `resolveNestedTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:338-379) is depth-agnostic: it walks `layout.blockParentMap` up to the outermost table (lines 342-348), finds that top-level table in `layout.blocks`, then rebuilds and descends the full nesting path (lines 366-379). So a block inside a table nested at any depth resolves, the branch returns a real line range, and `getWrapAffinity` (line 4150-4152, asking for the 'forward' reading) can answer 'forward'. This is corroborated by the todo checklist item (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-cell-hf-wrap-affinity-todo.md:63-67) and by an existing test asserting the typing path agrees with the click path at nesting depth 2 (packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts:297-324, notably the `expectForwardAffinityAtBoundary` call at line 323). The claimed inconsistency between the typing path and the click path at depth >= 2 therefore does not exist.
